Executable used for new interactive panes. Empty means SHELL, then /bin/sh; on Windows, pwsh.exe when present on PATH, otherwise powershell.exe.
Startup mode for new interactive pane shells.
CWD policy for new interactive panes, tabs, and workspaces.

Render pane images in Kitty graphics-compatible outer terminals. Set false to disable graphics rendering and the pane graphics API. Restart the server or reattach the client after changing it. In remote sessions, server configuration controls parsing and API availability while local client configuration controls outer-terminal output.

Update channel used by background version checks and herdr update. Stable Windows builds default to stable; existing Windows preview installs stay on preview until explicitly switched. Homebrew, mise, and Nix installs ignore the preview channel.
Check herdr.dev for new Herdr versions in the background.
Check herdr.dev for remote agent-detection manifest updates in the background. Bundled manifests and local overrides still apply.

Focus the next agent shown in the agent panel. Unset by default.
Focus an agent by index 1-9. Unset by default.

Create a new tab in the active workspace.
Rename the active tab.
Select the previous tab.
Select the next tab.
Move the active tab one position toward the front. Unset by default.
Move the active tab one position toward the back. Unset by default.
Switch to tab 1-9.
Switch to workspace 1-9 from prefix mode. Unset by default.
Close the active tab.
Rename the focused pane.
Open the focused pane scrollback in $EDITOR.

Clear the focused pane screen and scrollback, keeping the current cursor line and its visible soft-wrapped rows. Sends no input to the running program and does nothing on the alternate screen (for example, Vim). Unset by default; for example, clear_pane = "prefix+ctrl+k".
Suspend the focused pane's agent (graceful exit, native session reference kept), or activate it again when it is suspended. Unset by default; for example, toggle_agent_suspend = "alt+s".
"tabs" sidebar layout: prompt for a group name and move the focused tab there; a new name creates the group with this tab. Unset by default; for example, move_tab_to_group = "alt+g".
"tabs" sidebar layout: fold every group; once every group is folded, expand them all (the same toggle as the sidebar's ⏶/⏷ button). Unset by default; for example, toggle_groups_folded = "alt+e".

Restart the focused pane's live agent in place: graceful exit, then an automatic relaunch with its native resume command (agent.restart). A working, blocked or suspended agent is refused with a notice. Unset by default; for example, restart_agent = "alt+r".

Cycle the focused tab's color tag (tab.set_color): none, red, yellow, green, purple, then none again (a color set outside those four restarts at red). Unset by default; for example, cycle_tab_color = "alt+c".

Mark the focused tab important (tab.set_reminder), or unmark it; the tab menu's "Important" item does the same. The older name toggle_tab_remind is accepted. Unset by default; for example, toggle_tab_important = "alt+m".
Focus the News tab (news.open), creating it in the first space with the page viewer when it is gone. Unset by default; for example, open_news = "alt+n".

Open the Browser overlay: the herdr browser's profiles and tabs with who opened and last used each one; Enter focuses a tab's window, `s` starts or stops the profile, Esc closes. Unset by default; for example, open_browser = "alt+b".
Focus the coordinator tab, creating it (and starting the coordinator when it is enabled) when there is none. Unset by default; for example, open_coordinator = "alt+c".

Show or hide the focused tab's info pane: a dock on the right with the tab's agent-session notes (click to edit, tick task markers) and its history of checkpoints (decisions, milestones, failures, notes and bookmarks, each expandable to the prompt and reply around it). Open state is per tab; drag the divider or press < and > in the pane to resize. Unset by default; for example, toggle_info_pane = "alt+n".

Focus the tab you focused before, browser-style: back through every tab focus change (clicks, keys, agents' tab.focus, notification jumps), skipping closed tabs. A back or forward jump does not add a new entry; focusing another tab after going back drops the forward entries. The history is per client and forgets a restarted server. cmd is the super modifier; the terminal must pass it through (in Ghostty: keybind = super+[=csi:91;9u, or keybind = super+[=unbind). Inside a multiplexer that drops Cmd, bind another key, for example tab_history_back = "alt+," and tab_history_forward = "alt+.".
Focus the next tab again after keys.tab_history_back, skipping closed tabs. In Ghostty: keybind = super+]=csi:93;9u, or keybind = super+]=unbind.
Enter keyboard copy mode for the focused pane.
Focus the pane to the left.
Focus the pane below.
Focus the pane above.
Focus the pane to the right.
Swap the focused pane with the pane to the left.
Swap the focused pane with the pane below.
Swap the focused pane with the pane above.
Swap the focused pane with the pane to the right.
Cycle to the next pane.
Cycle to the previous pane.
Focus the last focused pane across workspaces and tabs. Unset by default.
Split pane vertically (side by side).
Split pane horizontally (stacked).
Close the focused pane.
Toggle zoom for the focused pane. The legacy key name `fullscreen` is accepted as an alias.
Enter resize mode.
Resize the focused pane toward the left. Unset by default.
Resize the focused pane downward. Unset by default.
Resize the focused pane upward. Unset by default.
Resize the focused pane toward the right. Unset by default.
Toggle sidebar collapse.
Modifier combo for tab shortcuts 1-9. Unset by default.
Modifier combo for workspace shortcuts 1-9. Unset by default.
Modifier combo for agent shortcuts 1-9. Unset by default.
Default expanded sidebar width in columns. Auto-scales based on workspace names.
Minimum sidebar width (columns) when expanded.
Maximum sidebar width (columns) when expanded.
Start Herdr with the sidebar collapsed. Changes take effect on the next launch.
Collapsed sidebar presentation.
Expanded sidebar composition. "spaces" stacks the space panel over the agent panel; "tabs" lists one row per tab across every space, in tab order.

Glyph at the right edge of a tab row in the "tabs" sidebar layout, keyed by canonical agent id, plus "other" (any other agent) and "shell" (no agent). Keys you omit keep their defaults. The keys "voice_live" and "voice_muted" replace the voice-mode mark (a live or muted microphone) of a tab whose agent is in voice mode.

Color of the focused tab row's agent glyph in the "tabs" sidebar layout, keyed like ui.tab_agent_glyphs. Values accept hex ("#rrggbb", "#rgb"), rgb(r,g,b) or named colors. Keys you omit keep their defaults; keys without a color, and invalid values, keep the monochrome glyph. Unfocused rows are always monochrome.

Minutes an important tab's agent (the tab menu's "Important" item, tab.set_reminder) may sit finished (unseen) or blocked before Herdr reminds you, then again every as many minutes until you focus the tab, the agent works again, or the tab is unmarked. The reminder is a notification for the tab's agent pane that follows ui.toast.delivery, replaces that tab's previous card and plays ui.sound.reminder_path (else the done or request sound) unless sounds are off. 0 turns these reminders off; values above 240 are clamped with a config warning. The settings overlay's reminders tab offers off, 5, 10, 15, 30 and 60 minutes. Scheduled reminders (the tab menu's "remind" selector) are not affected.

Local time of day (24-hour "HH:MM") a tab's daily reminder (the tab menu's remind selector, tab.set_reminder every = daily) fires. The settings overlay's reminders tab edits it too: its "daily at HH:MM" row opens a list of times in 30-minute steps (a configured time off that grid shows first as custom). A new time applies at once: if it is still ahead today the reminder fires today, otherwise tomorrow, and the change itself never fires one. A daily reminder missed while no client was attached fires once when a client next sees the tab that day. An invalid value reports a config warning and uses 09:30.

Default width in columns of a tab's info pane (keys.toggle_info_pane) until you drag its divider; a dragged width is remembered by the client. 28 through 120; out-of-range values are clamped with a config warning. The pane never takes more than 70% of the window and always leaves the terminal 30 columns; a pane surface narrower than 58 columns shows no pane until the window widens.

Show the Active block under the tab list in the "tabs" sidebar layout: blocked agents, agents in voice mode, working agents, idle agents with subagents running and finished agents you have not looked at, each with its time in that state. The block hides itself while nothing is active. Settings → indicators toggles it too.

Show the Pinned block under the tab list in the "tabs" sidebar layout: the tabs you pinned (tab menu → Pin), each with its status, team or group and time in state. A pinned tab also stays in its group. The block hides itself while nothing is pinned. Settings → indicators toggles it too.

Show the Scheduled block under the tab list in the "tabs" sidebar layout: the tabs with a scheduled reminder (tab menu → remind), each with its interval and the time to the next reminder (or the daily time), or fired while one is waiting. The block hides itself while no reminder is set. Settings → indicators toggles it too.
Terminal width at or below which Herdr uses the mobile single-column layout.
Capture mouse input for Herdr's mouse UI.
Automatically copy text selected by mouse drag or double-click. When disabled, Ctrl+C or a host-forwarded Cmd+C copies and clears the retained selection.
Host cursor policy.

Modifier that lets right-click gestures pass through to pane apps. Empty disables it. Accepts ctrl, alt, cmd, super, meta, hyper, or a + separated combination; shift is rejected because many terminals reserve Shift+mouse.
Force a full host-terminal redraw when the outer terminal regains focus.
Lines to scroll per mouse wheel notch.
Ask for confirmation before closing a workspace.
Ask for a tab name before creating a new tab.
Ask for a workspace name before interactive TUI creation.

Draw borders around split panes. auto draws them only for split panes, always also frames a lone pane (only while pane_outer_borders is enabled, since every edge of a lone pane is an outer edge), off disables them. Legacy booleans still parse: true maps to auto and false maps to off.
Draw borders along the outside edge of the pane area. Disable with pane gaps disabled for tmux-style internal splitters without an outside frame.
Draw interactive scrollbars beside terminal panes. Disable to reclaim the scrollbar column and keep it out of terminal-native selections.
Keep split panes visually separated instead of sharing divider borders.
Show agent labels in split pane borders when no manual pane label is set.
Hide the tab row when the workspace has one tab.
Place the desktop tab row above or below the terminal panes.

Configure ordered right-aligned tab bar entries. Supported types are zoom, hostname, datetime, text, and command. Command entries also accept lines (1-4, default 1: keep the last non-empty output lines; the tabs sidebar footer shows one row per line, the tab bar the last line) and ansi (default false: keep SGR color and bold/dim sequences for the tabs sidebar footer).
Text inserted between visible right-aligned tab bar entries.
Title Herdr writes to the terminal it runs in. Tokens: {hostname}, {workspace}, {tab}, {pane}, {terminal_title}. Empty leaves the outer title alone.
Agent sidebar ordering. Saved values are "spaces" or "priority"; "workspaces" is accepted as an alias for "spaces".
Choose compact color dots or distinct static symbols for agent states.
Blank terminal rows between expanded Agent sidebar entries. Set to 1 to restore the previous spacing.

Default expanded Agent sidebar layout. Entries may be token strings or inline { token, fg, bold, dim, rules } style tables. Text-valued built-ins and $name metadata tokens accept up to 16 ordered rules using equals, contains, starts_with, gt, or lt; the first match overrides specified styles. Text conditions optionally accept ignore_case for ASCII matching; numeric conditions require full finite numbers. state_icon accepts fixed styles only. At most 16 rows and 16 tokens per row.
Complete Agent-row overrides keyed by strict canonical agent id. Agents without an override use ui.sidebar.agents.rows.
Blank terminal rows between worktree groups and unrelated top-level Spaces. Worktree parents and their indented children remain packed.

Expanded Space sidebar layout. Entries may be token strings or inline { token, fg, bold, dim, rules } style tables. Text-valued built-ins and $name metadata tokens accept up to 16 ordered rules using equals, contains, starts_with, gt, or lt; the first match overrides specified styles. Text conditions optionally accept ignore_case for ASCII matching; numeric conditions require full finite numbers. state_icon and git_status accept fixed styles only. At most 16 rows and 16 tokens per row.
Accent color for highlights, borders, and navigation UI. Accepts hex (#89b4fa), named colors (cyan, blue), or RGB (rgb(137,180,250)).
Popup notification delivery. off disables popups, herdr shows in-app toasts, terminal asks the outer terminal for a desktop notification, system asks the OS notification service directly.

Seconds to wait before sending finished or needs-input agent notifications. Herdr notifies only if the pane is still in the same state when the delay expires. 0 is instant; valid values are 0 through 3600.
In-app toast position, relative to the full Herdr frame.

Keep in-app toasts on screen until they are handled instead of expiring. Cards stack from ui.toast.herdr.position, newest nearest the corner. Left-click focuses the card's pane and removes it, right-click dismisses it, and keys.open_notification_target focuses the newest card. A card also clears when its tab becomes focused, when its pane closes, when a needs-input agent is no longer blocked, when a finished agent starts working again, or when a newer notification for the same pane arrives.

Sticky cards drawn before older ones fold into one "+N more" line. The stack also stays within half of the frame height. Valid values are 1 through 20; values outside that range are clamped with a config warning.
Show the copied-to-clipboard popup after a mouse copy.
Copied-to-clipboard popup position.
Play sounds when agents change state in background workspaces.
Optional mp3 file path used for all notification sounds. Relative paths are resolved from the config file's directory.
Optional mp3 file path for "done" notifications. Relative paths are resolved from the config file's directory.
Optional mp3 file path for "request" notifications. Relative paths are resolved from the config file's directory.

Optional sound file for idle reminders (ui.idle_reminder_minutes). Unset, a reminder plays the "done" or "request" sound it reminds about. Relative paths are resolved from the config file's directory; on macOS aiff (such as /System/Library/Sounds) and caf, aif and m4a play too. The settings overlay's sound tab picks it, and done_path and request_path, from the macOS system sounds.
Sound override for detected Pi agents.
Sound override for detected Claude Code agents.
Sound override for detected Codex agents.
Sound override for detected Gemini CLI agents.
Sound override for detected Cursor Agent CLI agents.
Sound override for detected Devin agents.
Sound override for detected Agy agents.
Sound override for detected Cline agents.
Sound override for detected OpenCode agents.
Sound override for detected GitHub Copilot CLI agents.
Sound override for detected Kimi Code CLI agents.
Sound override for detected Kiro agents.
Sound override for detected Droid agents.
Sound override for detected Amp agents.
Sound override for detected Grok CLI agents.
Sound override for detected Hermes Agent agents.
Sound override for detected Kilo Code CLI agents.
Sound override for detected Qoder CLI agents.
Sound override for detected Qwen Code agents.
Sound override for detected Letta Code agents.
Sound override for detected Maki agents.
Sound override for detected Muse agents.
Resume supported AI-agent panes into their native conversation sessions when restoring a Herdr session.

Milliseconds between automatic agent restores after a server restart. The first agent starts without this delay; 0 disables spacing. Does not delay manual launches or explicit terminal attaches. Restart the server to apply.

Keep a copy of each open or suspended agent pane's native conversation transcript under the session directory (`agent-transcripts/`) and put it back before a resume if the agent has deleted its own. When false, no new backups are written; existing backups are still used before a resume. Herdr never deletes backups.

Run the AI news desk on a schedule: the server starts the bundled runner in a `News` tab at each local time in `news.times`. A desk that has never run (no run record, no edition) starts its first run as soon as news is enabled, at server start or when a config reload or `herdr news enable` turns it on, then follows the schedule. In the `tabs` sidebar layout the pinned News row shows whenever news is enabled, even before the News tab exists (a click creates it). Off by default; `herdr news run` starts a run by hand either way.

Local times of day (`HH:MM`, 24-hour) at which a scheduled run starts. Invalid entries are dropped with a config warning, duplicates collapse and the list is kept sorted. An empty list schedules no runs while `news.enabled` stays as it is. A slot missed while Herdr was off runs once on return when it was earlier that day and no run has started since; a manual run does not move the schedule. Replaces `news.interval_hours`, which now only reports a config warning.

Local wall-clock window `HH:MM-HH:MM` during which a news notification waits; it goes out when the window ends. Scheduling ignores it. May wrap past midnight. An empty string disables quiet hours; an invalid value reports a config warning and disables them.
Model name handed to the news runner (`claude -p --model`). Unset uses the runner's default.
Whether the herdr browser answers at all. When false every `browser.*` method returns `browser_disabled` and no Chromium is launched.
Start the default profile's Chromium with the server. Off by default: the browser starts on the first `browser.run` or `herdr browser start`.

Close the running browsers when the server stops. Off by default: Chromium is launched detached and survives herdr restarts and handoffs; the next server reattaches. Not yet honoured in v1a (the key is read and reserved).
The profile a call without `--profile` uses. Profile names are `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}`; an invalid value reports a config warning and `main` is used.

`auto` looks for `~/Applications/herdr+ Browser.app` (the branded copy `herdr browser install-chromium` makes), then `~/Applications/Chromium.app`, then `/Applications/Chromium.app`; otherwise an absolute path to a `Chromium.app` bundle or its inner binary. Google Chrome is not a fallback (different keychain item, different login store). A missing executable answers `browser_executable_missing` with a hint.
The node binary that runs the Playwright sidecar. Empty uses the one `herdr browser setup` recorded in `host/runtime.json`, then `node` on the server's PATH, the newest nvm node, then Homebrew's.

Extra switches appended to the Chromium command line. Automation and debugging switches (`--enable-automation`, `--headless`, `--remote-debugging-*`, `--remote-allow-origins`, `--no-sandbox`, `--disable-web-security`, `--user-data-dir`) are dropped with a config warning.
Relaunch a profile that has run before with `--restore-last-session`, so the tabs from before a quit come back.
Characters one page of `browser read` returns when `--max` is not given (2000 to 200000, clamped with a config warning). The footer names the offset of the next page.
Characters one page of `browser snapshot` returns when `--max` is not given (2000 to 200000, clamped with a config warning).
Long edge, in pixels, of the screenshot copy returned inline over MCP (256 to 8192). The full-size file is always kept.
How many herdr-named screenshot files are kept per profile under `shots/`; older ones are pruned. Files written with `--out` are never touched.
A browser tab or herdr pane touched within this many seconds counts as active in `browser.get` and `herdr browser status`.
Whether `browser eval` (arbitrary JavaScript in a tab) is allowed. When false it answers `eval_disabled`.
Whether the act family (`browser click|type|press|select|fill|hover`, and their MCP tools and batch steps) is allowed. When false every act answers `act_disabled`.

Whether agents may type, fill or press keys into a password field (`input[type=password]`, or `autocomplete` `current-password` / `new-password`, including the focused element for a bare `press`). Off by default: the sidecar answers `password_field_refused` and the agent is told to ask the user, who types it in the window (`browser focus`).

The activity window: a herdr tab whose pane used the browser within this many seconds wears the `◎` glyph on its row in the `tabs` sidebar layout, and its tab group keeps the `●` activity mark in its title and stays expanded for as long. The glow frame and cursor on the page fade sooner — the frame 15 s after the agent's last act, the cursor 5 s after the act that moved it — or at the end of this window when it is shorter (the pinned Browser row and its overlay show who is using which tab regardless).
How long a launch may take before Chromium answers on its DevTools port (3000 to 120000 ms). A launch that times out is terminated and retried once with a new port.
The default deadline of one browser operation (1000 to 600000 ms); `--timeout` and `browser wait` override it per call.

Show agent activity in the Chromium window: the tabs an agent pane opens or acts on sit in a tab group named after the agent and its herdr tab (the companion extension, loaded with `--load-extension`; its title carries a `●` mark and the group stays expanded while the pane is active, both gone after `active_glyph_secs`), and a purple glow frame with a gliding cursor is injected into the page — pulsing while an operation runs, a calmer steady glow after it, fading 15 s after the agent's last act (the cursor hides 5 s after the act that moved it), or at the end of the `active_glyph_secs` window when it is shorter. `false` turns all three off; a running profile needs a restart to load or drop the extension.

The symbol a tab group's title starts with, followed by the herdr tab label (the pane id when the tab has no label), keyed by canonical agent id plus `default` (any other agent, or a pane without one). Plain Unicode that Chrome's UI font renders; keys you omit keep their defaults.

Steer agents in herdr+ panes to this browser: the herdr-browser MCP server's instructions and, while `[agents] wrap` is on, `herdr agent wrap` carry a preference for the herdr-browser tools over the agents' own browser tools (Claude in Chrome, Codex's in-app browser / browser_use); web search stays fine for quick lookups. `false` keeps the neutral instructions.

While `[agents] wrap` is on, `herdr agent wrap <claude|codex>` turns the agent's built-in browser off for that session: Codex gets `--disable in_app_browser --disable browser_use`, Claude Code `--no-chrome`. Only affects sessions started through the wrap (the shell hook routes plain `claude` / `codex` in herdr+ panes to it).

Legacy: read only as a fallback for `[agents] wrap` when that key is unset. Setting the wrap from the settings overlay writes `[agents] wrap` and removes this key. Existing configs keep working unchanged.

Keep the herdr+ dashboard (the new tab page) as a pinned first tab in every normal browser window: the companion extension adds exactly one per window at launch, when a window opens and when herdr attaches, and removes duplicates and leftovers. A user who unpins or closes it is left alone for that browser session; it comes back at the next launch. `false` removes herdr's dashboard tabs. Applies live after `herdr server reload-config`; needs `show_activity`. The dashboard is never a tab in the ledger (not listed, grouped, overlaid or made current).

The agents whose herdr-browser MCP registration `herdr browser setup` (and the settings overlay's browser section) keeps: `claude` is Claude Code's user scope (`claude mcp add-json`), `codex` the `[mcp_servers.herdr-browser]` table in `~/.codex/config.toml`. An agent taken off the list is unregistered by the next setup or `fix all`; the registration itself is only ever written on that explicit request. Values other than `claude` and `codex` report a config diagnostic and are ignored.

Legacy and inert: kept so older configs parse. The shell hook (the guarded herdr+ line in `~/.zshrc` and its managed file) is installed from Settings → Agents after an explicit confirmation, or with `herdr browser setup --shell [--remove]`; plain `herdr browser setup` and the browser section's fixes never edit `.zshrc`.

The activity overlay's colour as `#rrggbb`: the frame border and glow, the cursor fill and the click ripple (the glow's transparency is fixed). Applies live after `herdr server reload-config` (the next overlay refresh uses it); an invalid value reports a config diagnostic and keeps the default purple. Tab-group colours are not affected: Chrome only offers its own nine named colours, and herdr picks one per pane.

Run the coordinator inside the herdr server: a Claude Code agent in a `coordinator` tab that watches the agents it manages, is woken when they message each other, finish or get stuck, and keeps a board of their state and its suggestions. The server starts it, relaunches it when it dies and serves its dashboard; there is no separate process to run. One coordinator per config directory: a second server on the same config directory reports `locked`. Off by default; `herdr coordinator enable` or the settings section turns it on. Disabling it stops wakes and the dashboard but leaves the coordinator's Claude running in its tab. Unix only for now; elsewhere the coordinator reports `unavailable`.
Model handed to the coordinator's Claude Code (`claude --model`). Applies at the next launch or restart. Unset uses Claude's default.

Most wakes the coordinator receives in a rolling hour. Past the cap the pending events wait and the coordinator row reads `capped`. The `HERDR_COORDINATOR_WAKE_CAP_HOUR` environment variable on the server process overrides it.
Most wakes the coordinator receives in a rolling 24 hours. The `HERDR_COORDINATOR_WAKE_CAP_DAY` environment variable on the server process overrides it.

Minutes after the last wake at which low-priority events that are still pending (for example an agent that appeared) wake the coordinator. Nothing pending means no periodic wake. Counted against the wake caps. The `HERDR_COORDINATOR_PERIODIC_S` environment variable (seconds) on the server process overrides it.

Most automatic relaunches of a coordinator that went missing in a rolling hour. Past the cap the coordinator is marked `down` with one notification; `herdr coordinator start` or Restart coordinator brings it back.

Show coordinator notifications: new suggestions on its board (batched into one), and the coordinator going down, blocked on a prompt, or locked by another server (once each until it recovers). The coordinator's own finished and needs-attention toasts are always silenced. Notifications go out only while a client is attached and wait for one otherwise.
Most new-suggestion notifications delivered in a local day; past the cap they are dropped. The `down`, `blocked` and `locked` alerts are not counted and never dropped by the cap.

Local wall-clock window `HH:MM-HH:MM` during which a coordinator notification waits; it goes out when the window ends. Only a `down` alert goes out inside it. May wrap past midnight. An empty string (the default) disables quiet hours; an invalid value reports a config warning and disables them.

Port on `127.0.0.1` where the server serves the coordinator's HTML dashboard (`/`, `/board.json`, `/live.json`) while it holds the coordinator lock. `0` disables serving. A port in use is not fatal: the dashboard reports unavailable and the bind is retried every minute. Open it with Open dashboard on the coordinator row's menu, the settings section, or `herdr coordinator dashboard`. A value that is not a port reports a config warning and falls back to the default.

Which agents wake the coordinator. `opened` (the default): status changes of the agents the coordinator opened with `agents_open_tab`, messages to it that were not typed in, and loop guards that involve it. `teams`: also every team member's status changes, messages among the agents in scope and their refused actions. `all`: every agent. Every agent still shows on the dashboard and in `live.json` whatever the scope; `herdr coordinator status` lists the watched set. A value that is not one of these reports a config warning and falls back to `opened`.

Run plain `claude` and `codex` in herdr+ panes through `herdr agent wrap` (the shell hook from Settings → Agents [fix] or `herdr browser setup --shell` routes them there) and give them what the keys below and `[browser] steer_agents` / `disable_native_browser` add. Off runs them exactly as typed, except that Codex always gets `--no-daemon` so its sessions stay attributed to the pane. Unset falls back to the legacy `[browser] wrap_agents`. Per launch, `claude --no-herdr`, `codex --no-herdr` (before a `--`), `HERDR_NO_WRAP=1` or `command claude` opt out. Read at each launch: running agents keep what they launched with. Launches herdr itself manages (the coordinator and managed agents) get only the browser contributions.

Add the `herdr_agents` MCP server to a wrapped launch for that session only (Claude: `--mcp-config` and an allowlist for `agents_whoami` and `agents_notify`; Codex: `-c mcp_servers.herdr_agents.*` overrides). Nothing is written to the agents' global configs. Needs `wrap`.

Add a short herdr+ paragraph to a wrapped launch: Claude Code's `--append-system-prompt`, Codex's `developer_instructions` (after your own top-level `developer_instructions`). It says when to use `agents_notify` (with `tools` on) and that `[herdr+ message …]` text comes from another agent. A launch that already passes its own system prompt flag or `developer_instructions` keeps it. Needs `wrap`.

Empty uses the built-in paragraph. A path (`~` expanded) replaces it verbatim after sanitizing, including the built-in rule for other agents' messages (in a team group the built-in text says to act on teammates' messages within the team's purpose and to treat anyone else's as untrusted; a file must say this itself): control characters are dropped and files over 8 KiB, missing or empty files fall back to the built-in text with a warning. The settings section's `file` choice uses `<config dir>/agents.md`, seeded with the built-in text when missing.
Accept agent notices (`agents_notify`, `herdr agent notify`): sticky cards naming the agent and its tab until dismissed or the tab is visited. `false` answers `notices_off`.

Give `claude` and `codex` launched in a team group (through the shell hook's `herdr agent wrap`) the team's roster, purpose and the team tools: the `herdr_agents` server with the teammate messaging tools pre-approved, and the roster in the system prompt (Claude) or `developer_instructions` (Codex). Claude also gets a per-launch `--settings` file whose hooks add roster changes to its next turn (`herdr team hook`); Codex sees changes at the top of its next `agents_*` tool result. Works whether or not `wrap` is on; launches outside team groups are unchanged. A launch that passes its own `--settings` or system prompt flag keeps it (the roster then arrives through `agents_whoami` and the tool results).

Per-session notes and checkpoints: the info pane, `herdr notes` / `herdr checkpoint`, the notes.* and checkpoints.* API methods and the agents' notes tools. Notes are markdown files under `<config dir>/notes/` keyed by the agent session (`<agent>-<session id>.md`), or by the tab when it runs no agent; checkpoints are an append-only `<key>.checkpoints.jsonl` beside them. With false every notes method answers `notes_disabled`; the files stay on disk. Independent of the coordinator. Wrapped and team launches get their notes and recent checkpoints back: Claude through a SessionStart hook (`herdr notes hook`: start, resume, /clear, compaction; herdr-started Claude agents too), wrapped Codex launches in their developer instructions at launch (not `codex exec`).

herdr adds checkpoints on its own, tagged `auto` and shown dimmed in the info pane: a bookmark for each prompt you send an agent, a milestone for commits made in the pane's repository during a turn (HEAD compared at turn start and end), and a failure when an agent stays blocked 10 minutes or more or exits mid-turn (not when herdr suspends or restarts it). They have their own hourly cap and never use the agent's. Needs `enabled`.
Root directory under which Herdr creates <repo>/<branch-slug> checkouts.
Add keepalive fallbacks and private connection reuse for `herdr --remote`. Set false to run plain ssh unchanged.
Maximum scrollback buffer size in bytes retained per pane terminal. The legacy key name `scrollback_lines` is accepted as an alias.
Allow launching herdr inside an existing herdr pane.
Deprecated compatibility key for terminal.kitty_graphics. Existing true and false values remain supported; terminal.kitty_graphics takes precedence when both are set.
Persist pane screen history to session-history.json.

Expose the focused pane's cursor anchor to the outer terminal even when the pane requested `?25l`, so macOS native input methods keep tracking the candidate window when TUIs paint their own cursor (Claude Code, pi, codex, etc.). Default: false.  When the pane reports no cursor position, falls back to the pane's top-left so a stable IME anchor is always available.  Trade-off when enabled: an extra hardware cursor will be visible in the outer terminal for apps that hide the cursor without painting a replacement (vim normal mode, etc.). See #149.

Restrict `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` to focused panes whose detected agent matches one of these names (case-insensitive). Empty list means apply to any focused pane. Unknown agent names are ignored; if the list contains no valid names, the reveal does not apply. Accepted names: pi, claude, codex, gemini, cursor, devin, cline, opencode, copilot, kimi, kiro, droid, amp, grok, hermes, kilo, qodercli, qoder, qwen, qwen-code, letta, letta-code, maki.
Cursor shape rendered for the IME anchor when `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` is enabled.

While prefix mode is active, temporarily switch the host input source to an ASCII-capable mode so prefix commands are read as ASCII even when an IME is active, then restore the previous input source when prefix mode exits. On macOS this selects the ASCII-capable keyboard layout; on Windows it switches the IME to English (ASCII) input. Windows support is currently limited to the Korean IME; with an IME for any other language, the input source is left unchanged. macOS and Windows only; a no-op elsewhere and a best-effort no-op if the switch fails.
